title: The Inaugural Ball
location: Grand Hall of the Republic, Ashenmere

narrative.text: The Grand Hall of the Republic has not seen a night like this in twenty-nine years. Crystal chandeliers cast warm light across a sea of formal dress and military medals. Every faction, every ambition, every grudge left over from the Halvek years is here — dressed in silk and swallowing champagne.
You stand at the top of the marble staircase, Jonas at your side. For a moment, the room turns. Faces lift. This is your first public appearance as Chancellor.
Six conversations you could have tonight. Six people who want something from you. The question is who you choose to speak with — and what that choice signals to everyone watching.

choices.text: Stay with Jonas. Tonight you are a person, not just a Chancellor.
Find Lucan Vael. He came to this ball for a reason.
Speak with Archbishop Renek. The Church's support will matter.
Find General Brenner. You want to know where the military stands.

narrative.text: You find a quiet corner near the east windows. The city lights of Ashenmere stretch out below. Jonas hands you a glass of water — not champagne. He knows you.
They are all watching you, you know. Even when they pretend not to.
Let them watch. Tonight I want five minutes of not being Chancellor.
You have about three. Vyktor is already moving through the room toward someone who looks important.
You both laugh. It is the first real laugh of the day.
Lucan Vael is exactly where you expected — at the center of a circle of businessmen, performing ease. He excuses himself when he sees you approach. That itself is information.
Chancellor. The Republic looks well on you. I hope the office will be — manageable.
I find most things manageable, Mr. Vael. What brings you to a government ball?
The same thing that brings everyone. To see what kind of government this will be. I think I am beginning to understand.
He means it as a compliment. You are not entirely sure it is one.

choices.text: Move on. The room is watching this conversation.

narrative.text: Archbishop Renek stands near the chapel alcove, as if the building itself has provided him a sanctuary. He does not come to you. He waits. You go to him.
Chancellor. The Church prays for this government. We have prayed for seventeen governments. We are patient people.
I hope patience will not be necessary, Archbishop. I intend to move quickly.
Speed and righteousness do not always travel together. But we will see. The Church is watching — with hope, not suspicion. For now.
General Brenner is not hard to find — he is the only person in the room who looks actively uncomfortable in formal dress. He is standing near the bar, not drinking.
Chancellor. I will be direct — I prefer it. The military has no political position. We serve the Republic. Whoever holds this office is who we serve.
I appreciate the directness, General. I intend to earn that service.
Good. Then we will get along. The Tyvaren situation — whenever you are ready to discuss it seriously, I am available. Not at a ball. In a room with maps.
You like him immediately. That is either a good sign or a warning.

choices.text: Schedule the meeting. Tonight is for appearances.
